'''Annemarie Surlykke''' (21 October 1955 – 28 July 2015) was a Danish [[physiologist]]. She contributed significantly to [[bioacoustic]] research, in particular in the fields of insect hearing and acoustic communication, bat [[Animal echolocation|echolocation]] and insect-bat interactions.

==Life==
Surlykkeg was born in Copenhagen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mindeord: Annemarie Surlykke |url=https://www.sdu.dk/da/om-sdu/fakulteterne/naturvidenskab/nyheder-2015/2015_08_03_surlykke |access-date=2026-05-26 |website=sdu |language=da}}</ref> She graduated from the [[University of Southern Denmark]]. From 1987 she was [[associate professor]] at [[University of Southern Denmark]] and [[Professor|full professor]] in 2011.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2015 |title=Obituary {{!}} Annemarie Surlykke {{!}} 1955-2015 |url=https://acousticstoday.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/Surlykke.pdf |journal=Acoustics Today |issue=Fall 2015 {{!}} |pages=197}}</ref>

In the 1980s and 1990s, Surlykke's research focused on ultrasonic hearing in [[Noctuidae|noctuid]] and [[Notodontidae|nothodontid]] moths. She later expanded to include [[Arctiinae|arctiids]], [[Geometer moth|geometrids]], [[Pyralidae|pyralids]], [[Sphingidae|Sphingiids]] and other nocturnal insects subjected to predation by bats. During this time, she also studied echolocation in bats. She conducted this research in the lab and in the field, leading into the 2000s and early 2010s.

Alongside her main work on insect and bat bioacoustics Annemarie Surlykke also contributed to the bioacoustics of [[odontocetes]], through cooperation with colleagues [[Bertel Møhl]] and Lee A. Miller.
